Hi Mateo,

Thanks for sending over the draft MSA and order form yesterday. Our broker had a quick pass and flagged a few items that will block procurement unless we reconcile them with your legal team. Main points:

- Cyber coverage: they can provide up to $1,000,000 cyber liability, not the $3,000,000 in your MSA. They asked whether SOC 2 Type II and a formal incident response plan would be acceptable in lieu of higher limits.
- Additional insured: broker wants the exact naming to be confirmed (which legal entity/entities to list).
- Primary / non-contributory and waiver of subrogation: broker needs to know if Redwood will require or accept either.
- Cancellation notice: broker typically provides 30 days; procurement prefers 60 days for enterprise deals.

I've attached the broker's checklist and their initial certificate stub for reference. Our target is to route countersignature by end of next week if we can agree on the insurance language.

Can you loop in your legal contacts and advise?

Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form - insurance questions from broker

Hi all — thanks for the context. I reviewed the broker checklist and Mateo's redlines. Below is a proposed path forward that balances Acme's procurement constraints with Redwood's risk posture.

Summary of proposed insurance language and concessions:
- Commercial General Liability: $1,000,000 per occurrence / $2,000,000 aggregate (no change).
- Automobile Liability: $1,000,000 combined single limit (if applicable).
- Employers Liability: $500,000 (as listed).
- Professional Liability / Technology E&O: $2,000,000 per claim / policy aggregate — required for SaaS/managed services.
- Cyber / Privacy Liability: Preferred: $3,000,000; Acceptable compromise: $1,000,000 provided Acme supplies BOTH (a) current SOC 2 Type II report and (b) a written incident response plan that names Redwood as a covered party for breach notifications/support. We will also require documented sublimits for PCI/PII if relevant.
- Additional Insured: For GL only, named as "Redwood Inference, Inc., and its affiliates" (we can provide final endorsement wording). We will not take Additional Insured on E&O or Cyber (standard).
- Primary & Non-Contributory: We request Primary & Non-Contributory for GL only; E&O/Cyber remain standard (non-AI).
- Waiver of Subrogation: Noted — we will accept waiver of subrogation for GL where permitted by law; cannot accept broadly across E&O/Cyber without underwriter confirmation.
- Cancellation/Notice: 30 days is standard from carriers; we can agree to use reasonable commercial efforts for 60 days but cannot force carrier-side commitments beyond 30 days. We will require the broker to notify us promptly of cancellations or material changes.

Recommended contractual text snippets (for final redline):
- "Vendor shall maintain Cyber Liability insurance with minimum limits of $1,000,000 per occurrence. In lieu of higher limits, Vendor shall provide: (i) a current SOC 2 Type II report; and (ii) a documented incident response plan that includes coordination with Customer and notification timelines."
- "Vendor shall name 'Redwood Inference, Inc., and its affiliates' as Additional Insured under the Commercial General Liability policy only via an ISO CG 20 10 (or equivalent) endorsement."

Next steps:
1) Acme / broker to confirm whether they can (i) issue a GL endorsement naming the entities as written and (ii) deliver SOC 2 Type II + IR plan.
2) If broker can only provide 1M cyber without SOC2, we will need underwriter confirmation or an exception from Legal/Finance (I can escalate internally).
3) If all OK, Stephanie — please proceed to update the Order Form wording and we will prepare the final MSA redline for countersignature.

I attached the MSA redlines and a short change log with the specific insurance clause edits highlighted.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.inference

Attachments: MSA_v3_redlines.pdf, MSA_change_log.txt

Hi Kimberly / Lisa / Mateo — this is Daniel Ortiz from SafeHarbor Insurance (Acme's broker). Quick update from our side:

- We can issue GL and E&O at the limits requested by Redwood. We can include Additional Insured language on GL via endorsement.
- Cyber: Acme's current carrier will only extend up to $1,000,000 for cyber at standard enterprise rates given their portfolio. They will provide a certificate showing $1,000,000 cyber and can provide an ACORD 25 certificate stub as proof.
- SOC 2 Type II: Acme does have an up-to-date SOC 2 Type II report and they can share it under an NDA/restricted access link.
- Naming: Broker proposes the following endorsement naming string — "Redwood Inference, Inc.; Redwood Inference Holdings LLC; and their respective affiliates" — please confirm if that satisfies your endorsement requirements or whether you need specific legal entity names listed individually.
- Cancellation: Carriers offer 30 days notice; we can request a best-efforts 60-day notice in the broker-carrier communication but cannot guarantee carrier-side contractual language beyond 30 days.

If Redwood accepts the compromise (1M cyber + SOC 2 + IR plan), we can prepare the COI and the GL endorsement and aim for delivery within 3 business days after receiving signed order form instructions.
